The agreement is a Master Professional Services Agreement for a $210k analytics platform for Harrington Health. The definitions section broadens the scope of "Losses" and incorporates extensive regulatory compliance (HIPAA, HITECH, etc.) that could increase AtliQ’s exposure. These clauses merit close review to limit potential liability and ensure compliance readiness.

It does not cover this client, despite the 27 Sep assumption that it 'should do'. The freelancer brought in for this client (Kriti Data Labs, C-037; Daniel Ortiz, C-047) has a contractor agreement and NDA in draft but no subcontractor BAA.

findings.title: Unlimited liability for AtliQ — no cap at all
findings.explanation: AtliQ's liability is expressly unlimited, for direct and indirect losses alike. The carve-out covers data-security / privacy events, where regulatory fines, notification and credit-monitoring costs are the largest exposure. By contrast §10.2 caps the other side's liability at THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID BY CLIENT TO CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT. AtliQ's position has been liability capped at 1x fees; Karandeep walked away from Kessler Mobility (~€120k) over 'liable without limitation'.
findings.contract_quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING CONTRACTOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF THE BAA, OR ANY DATA SECURITY INCIDENT.
escalation_hints: Consider counsel review (Calloway Stern LLP) — share this contract together with the cited signed agreements.
Healthcare / PHI: consider Calloway Stern review (they reviewed the CareBridge BAA).

findings.title: Uncapped liquidated damages — two percent (2%) of Total Contract Value per day
findings.explanation: Delay clause terms: two percent (2%) of Total Contract Value per day, no cap, no exclusion for client-caused delay, cumulative with other remedies. AtliQ's precedent is 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone, with no LD for client-caused delay (Acme Mar 2025, Northwind Jun 2025, Trustline Aug 2026). An uncapped LD on the full contract value is the Brightwater pattern — that contract had no client-delay exclusion either, and a 19-day client-caused delay produced an $18.4k claim and a $9k settlement. Nothing stops LD accruing while AtliQ waits on the client's own data or access. The only accepted 10%-of-total cap (Al Noor) was approved as a one-off exception, not a standard.
findings.contract_quote: Accordingly, if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.

findings.title: Payment in 90 days
findings.explanation: Invoices are payable in 90 days. AtliQ's stated position is '30 days, 45 max' (Karandeep's checklist) and Trustline's 90-day request was negotiated down to 45 days in Aug 2026. At 90 days AtliQ funds roughly a quarter of delivery cost upfront.
findings.contract_quote: Client shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within ninety (90) days after Client's receipt thereof.
escalation_hints: Check with Finance (cash-flow impact).

findings.title: Client can withhold disputed payments while work continues
findings.explanation: The clause lets the client retain payment for any disputed amount without a time limit, yet requires AtliQ to keep performing. This creates cash‑flow exposure, especially combined with the 90‑day payment term already flagged.
findings.contract_quote: Client may withhold payment of any amount it disputes in good faith. Contractor shall continue performing the Services during the pendency of any dispute.
escalation_hints: Check with Finance (cash-flow impact).

findings.title: Termination on 7 days' notice with no payment for work in progress
findings.explanation: The client can terminate on 7 days' notice and pay only for accepted deliverables — work in progress, unaccepted deliverables and demobilisation are unpaid. Karandeep's checklist: 'termination → they pay for work done'. Other client contracts pay pro rata for milestones in progress (Trustline, Acme).
findings.contract_quote: Client may terminate this Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, for any reason or no reason, upon seven (7) days' written notice to Contractor.

findings.title: Regulatory termination without compensation
findings.explanation: Client can terminate immediately if AtliQ is excluded from any federal health care program, potentially ending the deal with no payment for work performed. This unilateral right creates exposure to abrupt revenue loss.
findings.contract_quote: Client may terminate immediately if Contractor or any Contractor Personnel is excluded from participation in any federal health care program.

findings.title: AtliQ's pre-existing tools would be assigned to the client
findings.explanation: Pre-existing materials incorporated into (or needed to use) a deliverable are assigned outright to the client, not licensed. AtliQ's position: 'client owns what we build for them, we keep our own stuff'. This is how PipeKit was lost to Northwind (§9.2 there) — once assigned, AtliQ can no longer reuse or warrant ownership of the accelerator elsewhere.
findings.contract_quote: To the extent any Deliverable, or any Pre-Existing Materials incorporated into or necessary for the use of any Deliverable, does not qualify as a work made for hire, Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein, including all intellectual property rights, without further consideration.
escalation_hints: Check with Pranav (CTO) — IP reuse, delivery model or staffing.

findings.title: AtliQ would indemnify the client even for the client's own negligence
findings.explanation: The indemnity applies 'regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of' the client's indemnitees. AtliQ's standard is mutual indemnity — each side covers its own breach and negligence (PayTrack, Jan 2025: 'we can't insure against PayTrack's own negligence'). Combined with uncapped liability this exposure is open-ended.
findings.contract_quote: Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client, its Affiliates, and their respective trustees, directors, officers, employees, medical staff, agents, successors and assigns (the "Client Indemnitees") from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) the Services or Deliverables, (b) any breach of this Agreement or the BAA by Contractor, (c) any claim that a Deliverable infringes any third-party intellectual property right, or (d) any act or omission of Contractor Personnel, in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any Client Indemnitee.

findings.title: Contractor bears full breach remediation costs
findings.explanation: Clause 12.3 makes AtliQ responsible for all investigation, notification, credit monitoring and remediation costs after a security incident, which can be substantial and exceed typical insurance limits.
findings.contract_quote: Contractor shall notify Client of any actual or reasonably suspected security incident affecting Client data within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery and shall bear all costs of investigation, notification, credit monitoring and remediation.
escalation_hints: Healthcare / PHI: consider Calloway Stern review (they reviewed the CareBridge BAA).

findings.title: Requires $5M cyber cover — AtliQ holds $1M
findings.explanation: The contract requires cyber liability insurance of $5,000,000. AtliQ's cyber policy is $1M (Karandeep, tracker C-046 / Harrington huddle 27 Sep). Signing would put AtliQ in breach from day one unless cover is increased or the requirement negotiated. Other limits in the same clause: professional liability $5,000,000, umbrella $5,000,000 — AtliQ's PI/E&O cover is not recorded in the dataset; verify with the broker. The gap has not yet been raised with the client (meeting note 27 Sep).

findings.title: Overly broad definition of Losses
findings.explanation: The contract defines "Losses" to include any and all damages, liabilities, penalties, costs, and attorneys' fees, which could be used to expand AtliQ's indemnity and liability obligations beyond typical limits.
findings.contract_quote: "Losses" means any and all losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, claims, actions, judgments, settlements, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs or expenses of whatever kind, including reasonable attorneys' fees.
escalation_hints: Healthcare / PHI: consider Calloway Stern review (they reviewed the CareBridge BAA).

findings.title: Client‑driven personnel removal at no cost to client
findings.explanation: The client can unilaterally demand removal of any AtliQ staff and require a prompt replacement at no additional cost, potentially increasing staffing costs and causing project delays.
findings.contract_quote: Contractor shall assign qualified Contractor Personnel. Client may, in its sole discretion, request removal of any Contractor Personnel, and Contractor shall promptly replace such individual at no additional cost to Client. Contractor Personnel accessing Client facilities or systems shall complete Client's background check, drug screening, immunization and compliance training requirements.
escalation_hints: Check with Pranav (CTO) — IP reuse, delivery model or staffing.

findings.title: No deemed acceptance — invoicing depends entirely on the other side signing off
findings.explanation: Acceptance never happens by use in production or lapse of time, and the client may repeat testing or reject for a full refund. Since invoices follow acceptance, payment timing is in the client's hands. AtliQ's signed MSAs deem acceptance after 7–10 business days without written rejection.
findings.contract_quote: Acceptance shall not be deemed to occur by use in production, by payment, or by the passage of time.
escalation_hints: Check with Finance (cash-flow impact).

findings.title: Injunctive relief without bond
findings.explanation: Client may obtain injunctive relief against AtliQ without posting a bond, exposing AtliQ to costly injunctions even for alleged breaches where damages are hard to quantify.
findings.contract_quote: Contractor acknowledges that any breach of this Article may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be inadequate, and that Client shall be entitled to injunctive relief without the posting of bond.
escalation_hints: Healthcare / PHI: consider Calloway Stern review (they reviewed the CareBridge BAA).

findings.title: Restriction on third‑party components
findings.explanation: The client requires prior written approval before any open‑source or third‑party software can be used, which may limit AtliQ's ability to leverage standard tools and cause delays or extra cost.
findings.contract_quote: Contractor shall not incorporate any open-source or third-party software into any Deliverable without Client's prior written approval.
escalation_hints: Discuss with the vendor — AtliQ's own paper; PixelCraft precedent shows how it was softened before.

findings.title: Client‑directed re‑performance or refund
findings.explanation: Client may at its option require AtliQ to re‑perform non‑conforming services or refund fees, exposing AtliQ to additional labor costs and potential loss of revenue for work already performed.
findings.contract_quote: Contractor shall, at Client's option, re-perform any non-conforming Services or refund the Fees paid therefor.
escalation_hints: Check with Finance (cash-flow impact).

findings.title: BAA takes precedence over agreement
findings.explanation: The Order of Precedence clause makes the Business Associate Agreement (BAA) senior to this MSA. If the BAA contains liability or indemnity caps, it could conflict with the unlimited liability and indemnity provisions already flagged, creating uncertainty for AtliQ.
findings.contract_quote: In the event of conflict: (a) the BAA (as to PHI); (b) this Agreement; (c) the applicable SOW; (d) other Exhibits.
escalation_hints: Healthcare / PHI: consider Calloway Stern review (they reviewed the CareBridge BAA).
